St. Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea

Saints

St. Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea

St. Gregory Thaumaturgus · St. Gregory of Neocaesarea · St. Gregory the Wonderworker

Period
Third century; born between 210 and 215 in the OCA life
Region
Pontus; Neocaesarea
Titles / vocation
Bishop · Teacher
Commemoration
November 17

Introduction

A third-century bishop and missionary in Pontus. Thaumaturgus means Wonderworker; this St. Gregory is distinct from the later Cappadocian saints.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomTeaching and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Repose after episcopal service; exact date and manner are not given by this source

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA places his birth between 210 and 215 in a prominent pagan family at Neocaesarea. Originally called Theodore, he became a Christian and studied under Origen.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Opening biographical paragraphs

Life and notable events

He became bishop of his home city. The received life depicts preaching, care for the needy, reconciliation of disputes, and protection of Christians during the Decian persecution of 249–251. Its miracle narratives explain his traditional title.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Episcopacy, pastoral work, and Decian persecution

Death and martyrdom

The entry describes his repose after his episcopal ministry but supplies neither an exact year nor a manner of death. It does not narrate an execution.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Final biographical paragraph

Teaching and legacy

The OCA associates a Trinitarian confession with him and relates its reception by later Fathers. It also transmits the account that Christianity grew from a small minority to predominate in his city.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Symbol of Faith; concluding account of conversions

Chronology

  1. 210–215

    Birth range in the published life.

    [1] Official Orthodox life · Opening paragraph

  2. 249–251

    He shelters his flock during Decius’s persecution.
